{{Short description|Irish biological researcher (1938–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Tomás Mac Síomóin'''  (19 February 1938 – 17 February 2022) was an Irish doctoral graduate of [[Cornell University]], [[New York (state)|New York]], who worked as a biological researcher and university lecturer in the US and Ireland. He worked as a journalist, as editor of the newspaper ''[[Anois]]'' and for many years was editor of the literary and current affairs magazine, ''[[Comhar]]''. He wrote in [[Irish language|Irish]] and published both poetry and fiction in that language.

==Biography==
He was born in [[Dublin]]. His story ''Cinn Lae Seangáin'' (“The Diary of an Ant”) won the award for best short story collection in the [[Oireachtas na Gaeilge|Oireachtas]] 2005 competition, while in the following year his novel ''An Tionscadal'' (“The Project”) won the main Oireachtas literary award.

His poems, stories, articles and translations from [[Catalan language|Catalan]] and [[Spanish language|Spanish]] have appeared in diverse publications. His novel, ''Ceallaigh'' (2009), was written in [[Cuba]]; it challenges some common assumptions about contemporary Cuban life and history.

His work has been translated into many languages, most recently into [[Slovene language|Slovenian]], [[Romanian language|Romanian]] and Catalan. He lived and worked since circa 1998 in [[Catalonia]].

Tomás Mac Síomóin died on 17 February 2022, at the age of 83.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tomás Mac Síomóin: From One Bright Island Flown |last=Farrell |first=Jenny |via=[[ResearchGate]] |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388721585_Tomas_Mac_Siomoin_From_One_Bright_Island_Flown |access-date=10 June 2022 |publisher=Culture Matters |date=19 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tomás Mac Síomóin obituary: Irish Marxist writer with a hatred of neoliberalism |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/opinion/tomas-mac-siomoin-obituary-irish-marxist-writer-with-a-hatred-of-neoliberalism-1.4817500 |access-date=13 June 2022 |publisher=The Irish Times |date=4 March 2022}}</ref>
